summary: The ship repair task at unit+A20h. 00821E80's 9Eh add arm (0082205C / 008220A3) now runs the reconstructed adders 0093A4F0 (water) and 0093A470 (fire) over a task view of the gunnery host's DamageControl fields (+2Ch/+30h ticks, +34h water, +38h fire, new +3Ch fire total and +40h water copy, +44h = task.reported_repaired, which both adders clear), replacing the inline add; their pending-damage test (0090E6C0 tail) and the two adds were re-modelled per op at PC24 (x87_mul24 / x87_add24; listing 0093A489..0093A4CB and 0093A518..0093A54D), matching what the host's float code already computed. The script orders host now dispatches FailureRepairEnable (008AD540) through its body on a narrow base split out of Left55Seg56bHost (Left55FailureRepairEnableHost: vtable+5Ch and 00939FE0); the task address the body forms (entity+A20h) maps back to the host's id handle, and GameGunneryHost::set_failure_repair_enabled_00939fe0 calls 00939FE0 on a task view of task.failure_repair_enabled (+46h, read by 0093C520's failure step), kept across build_guns like the 9Fh hull flag. AddFire (008ACD10), an inert native that only reads its four arguments, is dispatched through its body instead of the unimplemented record. Validation: Win32 build and both CTests pass ON and with the switch temporarily OFF; tools/call_graph.py shows each body called from entry-reachable host code; readiness wired 9575 -> 9580. Not game-run.

review_round_1.finding: +3Ch/+40h drift: the timer steps zero them at expiry
review_round_1.detail: run_damage_control (ON arm) zeroes dc.water_last_40 when the stored difference water_seconds - dt is below 0 (0093C1A4..0093C1B9 test, 0093C1C3 store) and dc.fire_total_3c on the same fire test (0093C294..0093C2A9, 0093C2B3); verified in the listing. The OFF arm is the old four lines.

The DamageControl field comment names dc.fire_total_3c / dc.water_last_40 as the authoritative host copy. RepairTaskState's uint32 water_expired_slot / fire_expired_slot (whose fire/water labels on +34h..+40h are swapped against the adders' listing) are written only by the unlinked repair_task_update_0093ca20 sequence (call_graph: not in the exe) and by the revive reset, and are never read. Their revive resets were left in place: they are old code and harmless.
